thread:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-INC-4892 — prometheus-scrape: high scrape_error_rate (service=metrics-pipeline)

maria: saw this pop up, looks like a lot of scrape errors in us-west-2, not the usual pattern. ticketed PD-INC-4892 and auto-page went to the oncall list.

aj: I'm oncall, pulling logs now. quick glance: kube-scrape-proxy 503s and our log-queue ingestion lag increasing. can someone check router and kafka consumer lag?

samir: checking Kafka. consumer group `log-ingest-usw` shows ~2.1M messages lag. likely backpressure from s3-throttles last night. running `kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group log-ingest-usw` now.

jess: seeing a bunch of `503` from scrape-proxy in envoy logs. probable rate-limiting on the scrape endpoints. paste of recent error snippet:
```
2026-03-14T18:22:01Z envoy: upstream reset: 503
[metrics-scrape] request failed: HTTP 503 Service Unavailable
```

kyle: pd note — incidentbot tried to page, but we got a deferred/loop ack from PD due to the service token bouncing. I see `incidentbot` retried paging 3x. stack: incidentbot -> pd -> oncall -> back to incidentbot with a loopback. need to break the loop.

incidentbot: System note: page deferred due to RateLimit in PD integration. Attempts: 3. Status: partial-ack. See https://pagerduty.example/pd/PD-INC-4892

maria: ok, short term: put scrape-proxy into maintenance-mode for the noisy targets to stop the flood of alerts, then we can backfill logs once ingestion stabilizes. any objections?

aj: +1. I'll remove noisy targets from the scrape config via configmap edit and roll the scrape-proxy. quick command:
```
kubectl -n infra edit configmap scrape-proxy-targets
# remove customers with excessive 429s
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/scrape-proxy
```

samir: I'll scale up `log-ingest-consumer` by 2x for us-west to help drain the backlog. running:
```
kubectl -n ingestion scale deployment/log-ingest-consumer --replicas=8
```

jess: also recommend turning on KV cache bypass for long-tail prefixes to reduce repeated tokenization cost — will open a small rollout.

kyle: Pushing an interim PD annotation: "oncall acknowledged, throttling observed in scrape-proxy, scaling consumers and removing noisy targets. follow-up: ETA 25m. If customer-impact observed, notify Customer Ops." Adding customer-ops-bot to thread.

customer-ops-bot: Alerting customers: Draft message queued for impacted customers. Template: "We are experiencing delayed metrics and logs in [region]. Engineers are actively mitigating. No data loss expected; ingestion backlog being cleared. Next update in 30 minutes." Send? (react with :thumbsup: to send).

maria: :thumbsup: send it. Also, can someone check whether any downstream dashboards have alert rules firing that need muting? I already muted `dashboard-availability` in Grafana for a few noisy panels.

aj: muting done for a set of panels and a couple of alerts that were purely symptomatic. Confirmed: Kibana indexing rate is down ~60% during the spike.

samir: consumer scaling started, partitions are being rebalanced. lag dropping slowly: 2.1M -> 1.7M in last 4 minutes.

jess: rolled out config change to skip long-tail prefixes; this reduced CPU on scrape-proxy pods by ~30%.

incidentbot: PD update: Status changed to "Acknowledged by oncall". Auto-escalation suppressed due to maintenance window tag. (internal note logged)

kyle: quick postmortem note while it's fresh:
- root cause: S3 throttling in us-west triggered log ingestion backpressure -> downstream scrape-proxy started returning 503s for scrape targets -> Prometheus reported high scrape_error_rate -> PagerDuty fired
- immediate mitigations: removed noisy targets, scaled consumers, muted symptomatic alerts, sent customer notice
- next actions: backfill ingest queue, investigate S3 throttling origin (transfer jobs?), add circuit-breaker to scrape-proxy for noisy endpoints, fix PD integration loopback (token refresh handling)

maria: I can't stress enough we need PD retry dedupe: incidentbot's retries caused extra noise. opening a ticket to change incidentbot to exponential backoff + dedupe on PD incident key.

aj: agree. also, we should add an early-warning metric: `s3_throttle_errors` -> if spike, reduce scrape frequency automatically for affected targets.

samir: lag is now 1.2M and dropping. estimate 40m to drain at current rate. will monitor.

jess: starting a small backfill job in batch cluster with `backfill-consumer --max-parallel 6` to help reduce critical dashboards. watching for errors.

kyle: Customer Ops confirms message sent. They want a short summary once we have ETA < 10m.

incidentbot: System: PD incident PD-INC-4892 updated: status=resolved (manual close by oncall). Final note: ingestion lag reduced, customer notice sent. Logs show no data loss.

maria: thanks team. we'll keep this thread open for the drain and then convert to a postmortem doc. tagging @postmortem-owner (will be samir)

samir: pulling the timeline artifacts now and will start the PM template in 15m.

aj: good job. feel free to hand off to next oncall if needed. I'm dropping from the thread.

kyle: leaving a short runbook addition: if `log-ingest` lag > 500k AND `scrape_error_rate > 5%` then scale consumers + remove noisy scrapes + send customer notice.

jess: added runbook entry to `eng-sre/runbooks/metrics-ingest-runbook.md` (small PR).

maria: closing thread once backlog < 100k and dashboards stable. current backlog: 860k. next update in 20m.

aj: ack.

samir: 20m update: backlog 420k, no new 503s from scrape-proxy. starting to close noisy maintenance window in 10m.

kyle: agree to start re-adding targets carefully after 10m. if anything spikes, revert.

incidentbot: Thread closed by oncall. Summary appended to PD incident. :white_check_mark:
